wu: Goal Ball Toss: Students stand in a circle. Teacher tosses a soft ball to a student and asks, 'What's one goal you have for this year?' The student answers and tosses the ball to another student. Repeat for 3-4 rounds.
wuAlt: New Year Bingo: Students write 5 goals (e.g., 'study more English') in a grid. Teacher calls out goals; students cross off matches and shout 'Bingo!' when they have 3 in a row.

Goal Chain: Students stand in a line. The first student says, 'My goal is to learn English.' The next says, 'My goal is to learn English, and play football.' Each student adds one new goal to the chain.
pres: Teacher shows flashcards of goals (e.g., 'read more books', 'exercise', 'learn guitar'). Models sentences: 'I want to read more books.' 'I would like to exercise.' Elicits more examples from students. Checks understanding by asking, 'What do you want to do this year?'
presAlt: Goal Story: Teacher tells a short story about a character who sets goals (e.g., 'Fatima wants to learn English because she wants to travel'). Asks comprehension questions like, 'What does Fatima want to do?'
Goal Charades: Teacher acts out a goal (e.g., miming reading a book). Students guess and say, 'You want to read more books!'
prac: Goal Match-Up: Students receive cards with goals (e.g., 'study harder') and sentence starters (e.g., 'I want to...'). They match the cards to form correct sentences. In pairs, they practice saying the sentences aloud. Teacher monitors and corrects pronunciation.
pracAlt: Goal Relay: Two teams race to write sentences on the board. Teacher shouts a goal (e.g., 'learn guitar'), and the first student from each team runs to write 'I want to learn guitar.' The team with the most correct sentences wins.
Goal Chain Drill: Students sit in a circle. The first student says, 'I want to study English.' The next says, 'He wants to study English, and I want to play sports.' Continue building the chain.
ls: Goal Interviews Audio: Students listen to 2-3 short interviews where teens talk about their goals. They listen and write down 2 goals from each interview (e.g., 'Lina wants to learn French'). Teacher plays audio twice. Students compare answers in pairs.
re: Goal Jump: After the break, students stand. Teacher says a goal (e.g., 'I want to travel'). If the student agrees, they jump once. If not, they stay still. Teacher checks for understanding by asking, 'Why did you jump?'
prod: Pair Goal Interview: Students interview their partner using questions like, 'What do you want to do this year?' 'Why do you want to do that?' They take notes. Then, each student reports their partner's goals to the class (e.g., 'Sara wants to learn English because she wants to study abroad').
rw: Goal Self-Assessment: Students read a short text with strategy tips (e.g., 'Write your goals on paper'). They circle 3 can-do statements (e.g., 'I can talk about my goals'). Then, they write 2-3 sentences about their own goals using 'want to' or 'would like to'.
st: Teacher tells a short story about a teen who achieves their New Year goal. Then, leads a goodbye routine: 'Today we talked about our goals. Thank you for sharing! See you next week!'
g: Students write 5 goals in a grid. Teacher calls out goals; students cross off matches and shout 'Bingo!' when they have 3 in a row.
Two teams race to write sentences on the board. Teacher shouts a goal, and the first student from each team runs to write 'I want to...'. The team with the most correct sentences wins.
Students take turns acting out a goal (e.g., miming cooking). The class guesses and says, 'You want to cook more!'
Students stand in a line. The first student says, 'My goal is to learn English.' The next says, 'My goal is to learn English, and play football.' Each student adds one new goal.
Students receive cards with goals and sentence starters. They match the cards to form correct sentences and practice saying them aloud.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a short paragraph (40-50 words) about 3 goals and why they are important.
Support / weaker learners: Use sentence frames like 'I want to ___ because ___' to write their goals.
hw: Write 5 quiz questions about New Year goals for next class (e.g., 'What does Omar want to do this year?').
Draw a picture of your top goal and write 1 sentence about it.
Interview a family member about their goals and write 2 sentences in English.
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references (e.g., 'learn Arabic calligraphy') to make goals relatable. Encourage students to connect goals to local events like the Green March or Independence Day.
